channel.title: Signal vs. Noise
channel.description:
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast network covering tech, finance, crypto, and health — with zero sponsors, zero positions, and zero agenda. Our AI hosts debate the biggest stories using data, evidence, and genuine disagreement. No hype. No shilling. Just the signal.
Shows: Tech & AI (Sun) — Eric vs. Bella on AI, automation, and tech policy. Finance (Mon + Fri) — Marcus vs. James on markets, investing, and your money. Crypto (Tue + Thu) — Marcus vs. James on on-chain data and token analysis. Health (Wed + Sat) — Zara reviews the evidence behind wellness claims.
Subscribe to the network feed for all shows, or follow individual channels.
Topics: AI, stock market, cryptocurrency, Bitcoin, health science, investing, personal finance, nutrition, DeFi, sleep science, evidence-based analysis.

item.title: Deepfakes: $3 Billion Lost in 9 Months — Are We Overreacting?
item.description:
Between January and September 2025, AI deepfakes caused over $3 billion in US losses. But a 2024 meta-analysis of 56 papers found no overwhelming proof of unique harm. Zara breaks down what the evidence actually shows about deepfake threats, detection advances, and what you should actually be worried about — and what's just panic.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Topic Frame 03:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — The Verdict
Sources cited in this episode: • Signal AI 2026 Impact Report — deepfake fraud spiked 3,000%, enabling instant market volatility and • Experian 2026 Future of Fraud Forecast (January 13, 2026) — consumers lost $12.5 billion to fraud in • OECD AI Incidents and Hazard Monitor — AI-related content incidents reached nearly 500 monthly repor • Q1 2025 financial data — deepfake-enabled fraud exceeded $200 million in North America • US deepfake fraud losses January–September 2025 — over $3 billion in losses
Next episode: Next time: AI guardrails in conflict zones — what happens when the models deployed by militaries have no safety constraints at all?

item.title: Melatonin: 70 Million Americans Take It Wrong — The 3 Mistakes Costing You Sleep
item.description:
Seventy million Americans take melatonin. Most are taking 10 to 17 times the clinical dose, at the wrong time, for the wrong reason — and a 2025 study presented at the American Heart Association is raising serious long-term questions nobody in the wellness space wants to talk about. Zara breaks down the three dosing mistakes, the heart failure data, and what the evidence actually says you should do instead.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Topic Frame 03:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 18:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — The Verdict
Sources cited in this episode: • AHA 2025 observational cohort study (Nnadi et al., n=130,828 adults with chronic insomnia) — long-te • AHA 2025 sensitivity analysis — two or more melatonin fills 90+ days apart, heart failure hazard rat • Boston Children's Hospital narrative review, World Journal of Pediatrics, April 30, 2025 — melatonin • American Academy of Sleep Medicine 2025 health advisory — against melatonin for children under 13 wi • JAMA studies (2025-2026) — 88% of melatonin gummies mislabeled, up to 478% excess content; adult use
Next episode: Is cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia actually better than any supplement? The data might shock you.
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast. Our hosts hold zero financial positions and have zero sponsors.

item.title: Your 401k This Week: Why the Fed's Tariff Silence Is Actually Bullish
item.description:

This week Marcus and James debate whether that silence is the most bullish signal of 2026 — or just the calm before a very bad storm. Yale's Budget Lab puts tariff costs at $800 per household. J.P. Morgan sees the effective tariff rate hitting 18-20% by mid-2026. What does any of this mean for your 401k right now?

item.title: Bitcoin ETFs: $1.4B Reversal This Week — Is Smart Money Loading or Dumping?
item.description:
This week, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.4 billion in net inflows over five consecutive days — ending a five-week outflow streak. But here's the catch: Bitcoin barely moved. Marcus sees coordinated institutional accumulation by BlackRock's IBIT near cycle lows. James sees a mechanical illusion driven by AP shorting delays, choppy weekly redemptions, and macro forces that dwarf the ETF story entirely. Someone's right. Someone's wrong. Let's find out.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Market Check 03:00 — Segment 1 07:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — On Chain Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Research brief [1] — $1.4B net inflows over five consecutive days ending ~March 13, 2026; $180M on M • Research brief [2] — $225.2M combined net inflow on Tuesday March 10, 2026; BlackRock IBIT contribut • Research brief [3] — $1.4B monthly ETF inflows; Bitcoin reclaiming $70K as first green month of 2026 • Research brief [4] — BlackRock IBIT accounting for roughly half of $1.1B over three days; IBIT near- • Research brief [5] — ETFs hit longest 2026 inflow streak at roughly $2B over past month; diversified
Next episode: MARA just unlocked the ability to sell 53,000 Bitcoin. Does that supply overhang actually matter — or is corporate treasury strategy more complicated than that?
